original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Independently audit one link of the length-22 argument in PR #3058's f(7)=24 theorem: the claim that a 22-step restored seven-source word cannot have exactly 20 distinct prefixes. Re-derive the confinement obstruction as an explicit edge-count inequality on the five classified 20-point minimum covers, run the arithmetic completely for the two representatives where it decides the case, record bounded sampled evidence for the other three, and re-derive the two simple-cycle multiplicity patterns from the imported f(5)=12 and f(6)=16 values. No length-22 word census, no re-proof of f(7)=24, no frontier change.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a reported census pruning error invalidates a specific exclusion we still rely on and what bounded repair is justified. The predecessor package in this worker slot (research/f7-l22-split-domain, PR #3708) already derived the complete length-22 parity-split domain and handed off three bounded questions. The deciding downstream exclusion is now PR #3058's length-22 exclusion, whose |P|=20 step is the one that carries a set-level confinement claim rather than a census. Auditing that step is the bounded repair of the dependency boundary the card asks for, and it is a different deliverable from #2973's bit-0 prune reconstruction.
bottleneck_link: An unsound length-22 exclusion would wrongly close the f(7) question in the PR943 word model. This package narrows the reviewed dependency to two of five cover classes by arithmetic and states precisely which three remain sampled, so a later reader knows where to spend a complete replay.
stop_rule: Stop after the edge-count derivation, the five-representative arithmetic, the sampled component counts, the multiplicity-pattern re-derivation and the word-level search controls. No complete basis enumeration for representatives 1-3, no PR #3058 replay, no f(7) claim.
evidence: python3 -I -B research/f7-l22-confinement-audit/verify.py prints PASS_F7_L22_CONFINEMENT_AUDIT arithmetic_complete=2/5 sampled_only=3 f7_untouched in well under a second on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12. It rebuilds the twenty-point covers {0} u S from the five 19-point representatives in research/connector-covering-code/table6.json, requires each to satisfy P+P=F2^7, computes the seven largest difference multiplicities (21,21,21,14,14 against the 18 edges a two-component graph on twenty vertices needs), and therefore excludes |P|=20 for every basis in representatives 4 and 5 with no enumeration; representatives 1-3 are reported open with exact canonical-basis component counts 9, 12, 4 and deterministic 200-base sample minima 6, 5, 5. It also re-derives that a simple 22-cycle has exactly the multiplicity patterns (6,4,4,2,2,2,2) and (4,4,4,4,2,2,2) from the imported projections f(6)=16 and f(5)=12, and checks the recorded word artifacts: a universal 24-step word found by the package's own search (145164232614626031626540, 128/128, |P|=24, restored) as a positive control, plus two simple 22-cycles covering 126/128 and 125/128 as non-vacuity controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
